summary: GeoJSON is a geospatial data interchange format based on JSON. This proposed standard defines several types of JSON objects and how they combine to describe geographic features, their properties and their spatial extents. It uses a geographic coordinate reference system, WGS 84.

eli5.summary: This is a way to write places on a map, like a point for a city or a line for a river, as plain text that computers understand and share easily.

questions: what is the geojson media type
what coordinate system does geojson use
subtitle: A JSON format for points, lines, polygons and the map features built from them.

tldr.problem: Web applications needed a simple, shared way to exchange geographic data such as places, routes and areas using JSON.
tldr.mechanism: GeoJSON defines JSON objects of nine types: seven geometry types plus Feature and FeatureCollection, with coordinates given as longitude, latitude and optional height in the WGS 84 reference system.
tldr.outcome: It supersedes the original 2008 GeoJSON specification, drops the old crs member and registers the media type application/geo+json.

today: RFC 7946 is a Proposed Standard, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It supersedes the original 2008 GeoJSON specification.

sections.title: What GeoJSON Is
sections.content:
GeoJSON encodes geographic data structures using JSON (RFC 7159). A GeoJSON object may be a region of space (a Geometry), a spatially bounded entity (a Feature) or a list of Features (a FeatureCollection). A GeoJSON text is a JSON text holding a single GeoJSON object.

The format covers geographic data in the broadest sense: anything with qualities bounded in geographic space can be a Feature, physical or not. Its concepts come from existing open geographic information system standards, streamlined for web development. Its seven geometry types are the ones in the OpenGIS Simple Features specification for SQL.

The RFC says the specification, first published in 2008, has grown steadily in popularity, with wide use in JavaScript web-mapping libraries, JSON-based document databases and web APIs. This document supersedes the original 2008 specification.
sections.eli5: It is a way to describe things on a map using the same kind of text that websites already use, like writing the address of a treasure in a note.

sections.title: Geometry, Feature and FeatureCollection
sections.content:
Every GeoJSON object has a type member whose value MUST be one of nine case-sensitive strings: Point, MultiPoint, LineString, MultiLineString, Polygon, MultiPolygon, GeometryCollection, Feature or FeatureCollection. It MAY also have a bbox member.

A Geometry other than a GeometryCollection has a coordinates array whose shape depends on the type. A GeometryCollection instead has a geometries array of Geometry objects, which may be empty. A Feature has a geometry (a Geometry, or null if the Feature is unlocated) and a properties member (any JSON object, or null). If the Feature has a commonly used identifier, it SHOULD be given as id, a string or number. A FeatureCollection has a features array of Features, possibly empty.

Despite the word 'Collection', the features and geometries members are ordered JSON arrays, not unordered sets.
sections.eli5: A geometry is a shape, like a dot or a line. A feature is a shape with a name tag and notes attached. A feature collection is a folder of those.

sections.title: Positions and Geometry Shapes
sections.content:
A position is the basic building block: an array of two or more numbers. The first two are longitude and latitude (or easting and northing), in that order, and altitude or elevation MAY be a third element. Implementations SHOULD NOT add more than three elements, because the meaning of extras is unspecified and ambiguous. Parsers MAY ignore them.

The shapes nest as follows. Point is one position; MultiPoint and LineString are arrays of positions (a LineString needs two or more); Polygon and MultiLineString are arrays of rings or line arrays; MultiPolygon is an array of Polygon coordinate arrays.

A line between two positions is a straight Cartesian line in the coordinate reference system, which may differ markedly from the geodesic path over the curved surface. A linear ring is a closed LineString of four or more positions whose first and last positions are identical. A Polygon's first ring MUST be the exterior ring and any others interior rings (holes). Rings MUST follow the right-hand rule: exterior counterclockwise, holes clockwise. For backwards compatibility, parsers SHOULD NOT reject polygons that do not follow it.
sections.eli5: A spot on a map needs two numbers, how far across and how far up, like finding a square on a game board. A line is a list of spots, and a shape is a line that comes back to where it started.

sections.title: Coordinates, Bounding Boxes and the Antimeridian
sections.content:
All GeoJSON coordinates use a geographic coordinate reference system based on the World Geodetic System 1984 (WGS 84) datum, with longitude and latitude in decimal degrees. An optional third element is the height in meters above or below the WGS 84 reference ellipsoid. The old ability to use other coordinate systems was removed because it caused interoperability problems, although parties with a prior arrangement can still use alternatives.

A bbox array has length 2*n for n dimensions, with all axes of the southwest point followed by all axes of the northeast point, so a 2D box is [west, south, east, north]. A box that crosses the antimeridian has a northeast longitude less than its southwest longitude; the RFC's Fiji example is [177.0, -20.0, -178.0, -16.0], covering 5 degrees of longitude. Implementers MUST NOT use latitudes above 90 or below -90 to imply anything other than a spherical cap.

Geometries that cross the antimeridian SHOULD be cut in two so neither part crosses it, for example a line from 170 degrees E to 170 degrees W becomes a MultiLineString.
sections.eli5: Everyone measures from the same place on the globe, so a point means the same thing to every map program. A bounding box is a rectangle drawn around everything to show roughly where it is.

sections.title: Extending GeoJSON and Versioning
sections.content:
Members not defined in the RFC are called foreign members. They MAY appear, but there is no normative processing model for them, so relying heavily on them can reduce interoperability. GeoJSON semantics do not apply to foreign members or their descendants: a centerline member shaped like a LineString is not treated as a Geometry.

The fixed set of GeoJSON types MUST NOT be extended, and the meaning of existing members and types MUST NOT be changed. For example, FeatureCollection and Feature objects MUST NOT contain coordinates or geometries, and Feature and Geometry objects MUST NOT contain features.

There is no explicit versioning scheme. A specification that alters GeoJSON semantics or modifies the format creates an entirely new format that MUST NOT be identified as GeoJSON.
sections.eli5: You can add your own sticky notes to the map file, but you cannot change what the official words mean, or invent a new kind of official shape.

sections.title: Interoperability and geo URIs
sections.content:
GeoJSON texts should follow the Internet JSON (I-JSON) constraints from RFC 7493 for maximum interoperability. Text size matters: increasing coordinate precision from 6 to 15 decimal places can inflate a text with many detailed polygons by almost a factor of two, while 6 decimal places amounts to about 10 centimeters. The RFC also warns that the number of digits in coordinates MUST NOT be read as a sign of uncertainty. GeometryCollections should be used sparingly: nested ones SHOULD be avoided, as should collections of a single part or single type where a simpler geometry works.

A precise geo URI from RFC 5870 maps to a GeoJSON Point, so geo:lat,lon corresponds to a Point with coordinates [lon, lat], and an altitude maps to a third element. Uncertain geo URIs cannot be mapped because GeoJSON has no concept of uncertainty.
sections.eli5: Writing a place with a huge number of decimals makes the file bigger without making the place more exact, like measuring your desk in atoms.

sections.title: Security and the Media Type
sections.content:
GeoJSON shares the security issues common to JSON and provides no executable content. It offers no privacy or integrity services, so those must come from the transport, such as TLS or HTTPS. Location data about sensitive persons, animals, habitats or facilities can expose them to tracking or injury, and obscuring locations is unlikely to stop a determined attack.

The IANA section registers the media type application/geo+json, with file extensions .json and .geojson. The older application/vnd.geo+json entry should be marked OBSOLETED with a pointer to the new type.
sections.eli5: A map file that shows where a rare animal nests could help the wrong people find it, so share that kind of map carefully.
